picked.t: Samsung Vietnam reports $2.3B profit in H1
picked.body: Samsung Thai Nguyen, Samsung Electronics Vietnam (Bac Ninh), Samsung Display Vietnam (Bac Ninh), and Samsung Electronics HCMC CE Complex posted combined revenues of $35.2 billion in the period, up 21%, according to Samsung's latest financial report. Samsung Thai Nguyen, which manufactures mobile phones and telecommunications equipment, reported the highest revenues and profits, $16.2 billion and $1.08 billion, among the four units. The figures represented increases of 22.4% and 33.4%. Another phone factory, Samsung Electronics Vietnam, was second in terms of revenues, at $9.1 billion, while its profits topped $670 million. Roh Tae Moon, CEO of Samsung Electronics, said these two phone factories in the northern region, after 17 years in Vietnam, achieved cumulative exports of US$500 billion as of the end of June. Samsung Display Vietnam also reported increases in revenues and profits. Samsung Electronics HCMC CE Complex was the only one of the four to report a decline in profits, which fell from $180 million to $160 million. Samsung is South Korea's largest privately owned conglomerate, with core businesses spanning electronics, finance, heavy industry and technology. Starting with a television manufacturing plant in HCMC in 1995, it has become Vietnam's largest foreign-owned business with investments exceeding $24 billion as of the end of 2025. Globally, Samsung reported sales of $206 billion and profits of $80 billion for the first half of 2026, representing increases of two and nine times from the same period last year. China was its largest market, generating $59.7 billion in revenues and surpassing the U.S. and the Americas, which reported sales of $47.6 billion. Analysts say Samsung's surge in profits has been driven by storage and memory chips as artificial intelligence applications, particularly AI agents, expand into tasks requiring greater computing capacity.

picked.t: Russia, Philippines among fastest growing tourist markets for Vietnam
picked.body: The rise in Russian tourists has made Russia the largest European market and the third largest source of international arrivals to Vietnam this year, with around 1 million visitors, only after mainland China (3.5 million) and South Korea (2.8 million). Nguyen Tien Dat, CEO of AZA Travel, said: "Russian tourists enjoy swimming, sunbathing, eating seafood, and relaxing at resorts. Vietnam fully meets these needs, so it is understandable why they are visiting in large numbers," Dat says. Kristina Zagumennaya, director of a Russian travel agency, told the Russian news agency Sputnik in early August that Russian tourist flows are shifting between markets. While Turkey remains the top choice, Vietnam and China have recorded outstanding growth. "Vietnam stands out as a popular choice this tourist season," Zagumennaya said, noting that multiple charter flights are operating to destinations across the country to meet demand for both beach holidays and cultural tourism. In addition to charter flights, Vietnam Airlines increased the frequency of its direct Hanoi-Moscow route from three to four flights per week starting in July. Ranking behind Russia, the Philippines also showed notable growth, despite not being a prominent source market for Vietnamese tourism prior to 2025. Filipino visitors have risen to nearly 470,000 this year, among the 10 largest group of foreign visitors to Vietnam. Bui Thanh Tu, marketing director of BestPrice Travel, attributes this rise to more convenient flight routes, especially from Manila and Cebu, competitive costs, and tourism products that differ from the island destinations familiar to Filipinos. He also cites the viral impact of TikTok and YouTube videos featuring Hanoi, Sa Pa, Da Nang, and Hoi An. However, he notes that the strong growth was partly due to a low base last year, and says Vietnam needs to continue expanding air routes and developing suitable tourism products to sustain growth over the long term. In terms of overall volume of visitors in the first eight months, Asia remains the dominant region. Mainland China, South Korea, and Taiwan contributed around 6.2 million arrivals, accounting for nearly 40% of all international visitors to Vietnam.

picked.t: Vietnam megacity with 11.3 million motorbikes is stacking its roads four levels high
picked.body: The Cat Lai T-junction interchange sits on Hanoi Highway in Binh Trung Ward, connecting to Mai Chi Tho Boulevard. The Ben Thanh-Suoi Tien metro line crosses overhead, creating a three-level interchange. It is one of the busiest and most important routes at the city's eastern gateway, linking Ho Chi Minh City with the southeastern provinces and the north. Following the merger with Vung Tau and Binh Duong last year, Ho Chi Minh City now has nearly 12.7 million vehicles, including more than 1.4 million cars and 11.3 million motorbikes, the largest fleet of any locality in the country. Several arterial roads in the center and near the airport and ports carry heavy volumes and require multi-level interchanges to separate traffic streams and reduce congestion. The Cat Lai interchange opened in 2010 with two overpasses carrying left-turning traffic from Cat Lai Port, the country's largest, toward the city center along Nguyen Thi Dinh Street and Mai Chi Tho Boulevard, one overpass carrying left-turning traffic from the former Thu Duc City toward the port, and seven surface branches below. The bridge branches, surface roads and metro line interweave to form a modern traffic network at the city's eastern gateway. The bridge branches, surface roads and metro line interweave to form a modern traffic network at the city's eastern gateway. About 10 km away, the Tram 2 overpass is another key junction at the eastern gateway. Completed in 2004 at a cost of roughly VND120 billion (US$4.6 million), it connects Hanoi Highway with National Highway 1A for access to the city center or out to Dong Nai City. It was Vietnam's first cloverleaf overpass design, with four loops 420 m in diameter and connecting branches spread across 27 hectares. Two open-top underpasses, an overpass and the metro line stack up to make it a four-level interchange. Also on Hanoi Highway is the Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City interchange, completed in 2019. The project runs nearly 2 km and includes one open-top tunnel and three overpasses, stretching from the entrance of Suoi Tien theme park to near the new Mien Dong bus station. The open-top tunnel is more than 1 km long, with eight lanes and an 80 kph speed limit. Above it sit overpasses 17 m wide and 38 m long that allow vehicles to turn around. The metro line crosses overhead, forming a three-level interchange in the university district. The VND3.64 trillion ($138 million) project is part of the wider expansion of Hanoi Highway at the city's eastern gateway. After four years of construction, several components are already in use, including the overpass branch for right-turning traffic from the Long Thanh-Dau Giay Expressway down to Mai Chi Tho Boulevard, two bridge branches linking Mai Chi Tho with Dong Van Cong Street in both directions, and two underpasses on Mai Chi Tho that have helped ease local congestion. Contractors are now concentrating on the section connecting Mai Chi Tho with the expressway and Luong Dinh Cua Street. The full project is scheduled for completion in the third quarter of 2027. picked.t: Hanoi launches real-time flood map with instant alerts
picked.body: All data is extracted directly from an automatic monitoring station system managed and operated by Hanoi Sewerage and Drainage Company Limited. Rainfall conditions and floodwater depths are updated continuously in real time, with rainfall measured to the millimeter and water depth to the meter. The map uses a standard color scale to provide a visual assessment, enabling residents to gauge the level of danger within seconds. The application is expected to strengthen the capital's disaster response capacity while helping residents plan safer routes during the rainy and stormy season. The mini app is embedded directly into iHanoi, which already has 6.484 million registered accounts. This "all-in-one" model enables users to access potentially life-saving information immediately without having to install a separate application, saving device storage space and reducing access time on both Android and iOS devices. The application can also proactively send alerts directly to users' phones, meaning they can receive notifications without opening the app. When flooding or heavy rainfall occurs within a user's designated area, the system automatically displays a detailed pop-up alert, enabling residents to change their routes proactively. Users can set an alert radius ranging from 1km to 100km from their current location. They can also set specific hours for receiving notifications to avoid being disturbed outside their normal daily routines or at night. The map helps users avoid accidents caused by submerged manholes, potholes and fast-flowing water, while minimizing vehicle repair costs resulting from engine failure and damage to property. Location and notification permissions are clearly displayed, allowing users to choose whether to grant access. Even without granting location access, the mini app can still be used in basic map-search mode. The map is designed to serve millions of residents, drivers and visitors across the capital. Office workers and students, for example, can select routes that avoid flooded areas before leaving home. Ride-hailing drivers, delivery workers and truck drivers can protect their vehicles and cargo while avoiding breakdowns caused by floodwater. Households in low-lying areas can use the information to move belongings and vehicles to safer locations in anticipation of heavy rain. Transport and logistics businesses can adjust their routes based on real-time conditions, while disaster response agencies can gain an overall picture of the situation and respond more quickly. Residents can start using the service in three simple steps: download and open the iHanoi app; grant location and notification permissions to receive alerts relevant to their area; and set an appropriate alert radius and notification schedule to suit their daily routines. The launch of the map on iHanoi marks a new step forward in smart urban governance and disaster prevention in the capital. The deployment of advanced technology, combined with proactive action by the authorities, has the potential to change the way millions of residents respond to natural disasters.

picked.t: UK universities rush to cut tuition fees to win back international students amid decline
picked.body: At least 22 universities now provide automatic tuition-fee discounts to postgraduate taught students, with no separate application required, according to a review of 90 institutions by consultancy S Squared Insights, as cited by The Telegraph . Unlike traditional scholarships, students do not need to apply for or compete for these discounts. The reductions are automatically deducted from their tuition fees, with the amount varying by institution. Among them, the University of Aberdeen announced on its website it is granting international students a direct discount of up to £8,000, the largest reduction recorded so far. The University of Kent is offering a £5,000 tuition reduction for master’s programs to students from 14 countries and territories, including China, South Korea and Vietnam. The University of Nottingham, a member of the Russell Group of leading research universities in the U.K., is offering a £3,000 reduction. The Financial Times quoted Julian Westwood, director of S Squared Insights, as saying that universities had "shifted from smaller scholarship schemes to broad, overly simple cohort discounts." He warned that simultaneously facing declining student numbers and reduced per-student revenue could push some university financial plans beyond their stress-testing limits. Echoing these concerns, Zeenat Fayaz, founder of The Brand Education, told The Telegraph that this "pricing war" could backfire by forcing universities to compete on cost rather than educational strength. Fayaz noted that higher-tariff universities are also reducing grade requirements to admit more students, describing the escalating situation as "a race to the bottom." These discounts emerge as universities face intensifying competition to attract overseas applicants. International students pay higher fees than domestic students and provide a crucial source of revenue for the education sector. But their number has been going down. Latest Home Office data shows that applications for sponsored study visas fell by 11% to 381,500 in the year ending July 2026 , compared with the previous 12-month period. This decline in international recruitment largely follows the government's introduction of restrictions in January 2024, which prevent most overseas students from bringing family members to the U.K. There were 19,200 applications from student dependants in the year ending July 2026, a 6% drop from the previous year and a staggering 87% plunge compared with December 2023, before the restrictions took effect. According to the Office for Students (OfS), tuition fee revenue from postgraduate students stood at around £5 billion in the 2024-25 academic year, down £500 million from the previous year. In May, the Education Committee, a select committee of the U.K. House of Commons that checks and reviews the work of the Department for Education, warned that the government has no clear plan for universities facing insolvency. The committee warns that the U.K.'s higher education sector is under "unprecedented" financial pressure. These financial challenges are already having serious consequences, including staff redundancies, closures of courses and departments, recruitment freezes, and the selling off of assets. A total of 124 institutions, or 45% of the sector, could face budget deficits in the 2025-26 financial year without measures to mitigate the risks, compared with 96 providers that previously forecast a deficit in 2025-26. "Currently, there is no clearly understood protocol for how the government might respond to a situation of a provider at risk of imminent insolvency, which is a very serious problem," the committee said, as posted on the U.K. Parliament website. The U.K. had around 685,000 international students in the 2024-25 academic year. Average tuition fees for international master's students range from £15,000 to £45,000 per year, according to study-abroad consultancy ApplyBoard.

picked.t: Vietnam posts record $770B trade turnover in 8 months
picked.body: During the period, the country's exports rose 22.4% year on year to $374.84 billion, while its imports increased 35.3% to $395.3 billion, resulting in a trade deficit of $20.46 billion, according to data released by the National Statistics Office on Thursday. Exports reached $374.84 billion, up 22.4% year-on-year. The domestic sector accounted for $74.47 billion, up 7.4% and representing 19.9% of total exports, while the foreign-invested sector contributed $300.37 billion, up 26.9% and accounting for 80.1%. A total of 33 export items posted a turnover of more than $1 billion each, together accounting for 93.6% of total shipments. Seven products recorded export turnover exceeding $10 billion each, making up 70% of the total. Manufactured industrial products dominated exports at $337.99 billion, or 90.2% of the total, followed by agricultural and forestry products at $26.65 billion (7.1%), seafood at $8 billion (2.1%) and fuels and minerals at $2.2 billion (0.6%). Imports totaled $395.3 billion, up 35.3% year-on-year. The domestic sector accounted for $105.07 billion, up 23.7%, and the foreign-invested sector, $290.23 billion, up 40.1%. There were 43 import items worth more than $1 billion each, accounting for 93.9% of total import turnover. Three items exceeded $10 billion, making up 55.5%. Production inputs accounted for $372.04 billion, or 94.1%, of the imports. Machinery, equipment, tools and spare parts represented 57.6%, while raw materials, fuels and other inputs made up 36.5%. Consumer goods accounted for $23.26 billion, or 5.9%. The U.S. remained Vietnam’s largest export market, with turnover reaching $122 billion, while China was the largest import market with a turnover of $161.9 billion. In August alone, Vietnam's total trade turnover stood at $109.7 billion, down 0.1% from the previous month but up 31.7% year-on-year. Exports reached $54.79 billion, up 3.2% month-on-month. The domestic economic sector contributed $10.5 billion, up 2.2%, while the foreign-invested sector, including crude oil, recorded $44.29 billion, up 3.4%. Compared with August 2025, exports increased 26%, with the domestic sector rising 14.1% and the foreign-invested sector 29.2%. Meanwhile, imports in August were valued at $54.91 billion, down 3.1% from the previous month but up 37.9% year-on-year. The domestic sector recorded $12.82 billion, down 7.1%, while the foreign-invested sector reached $42.09 billion, down 1.8%. To boost exports, Nguyen Thi Huong, the office's general director, recommended the government effectively implement measures to promote exports and trade, diversify supply and production chains and import-export markets, and improve product quality. She also called for more effective use of opportunities from signed free trade agreements, stronger exports to major markets, and greater access to new and promising markets, including Halal, Latin American and African markets, with a view to achieving a sustainable trade surplus. Authorities should also provide enterprises with information and support to meet new market standards, assist them in anti-dumping cases, facilitate access to capital, and encourage the application of advanced technologies to improve product quality and value, thereby expanding markets and promoting exports, she added.

picked.t: 로투비(Law2B) 김유호 대표변호사, KBS 라디오 '한민족 하나로' 출연
picked.body: 베트남 사법연수원에서 강의를 하던 김유호 변호사 [베트남코리아타임즈] (호치민=베트남코리아타임즈) 앨런 리 기자 = 베트남에서 17년 넘게 한국 기업과 교민들의 법률문제를 다뤄온 로투비(Law2B) 김유호 대표변호사가 9월 4일(금) KBS 라디오 '한민족 하나로'(진행 이언경)에 출연해, 베트남 진출 기업과 교민들이 알아야 할 법률·생활법률 정보를 전했다. 김 변호사는 미국 UC 버클리대와 플로리다대 로스쿨을 우등 졸업하고 미국 변호사 자격을 취득한 뒤, 베트남 현지 로펌과 한국·글로벌 로펌을 거쳐 17년 넘게 베트남 현지에서 활동해 왔다. 현재 베트남 법무부에 공식 등록된 외국 변호사이자 로투비 대표변호사로, 저서 『베트남 투자·창업자가 꼭 알아야 할 베트남 법』과 『꼭 알아야 할 베트남 생활법률 가이드』를 통해 실무 경험을 정리한 바 있다. 이번 방송에서는 ▲WTO 가입 직후 베트남 진출 초기의 시장 상황과 한인·기업 분위기 ▲미국 변호사 자격 취득 후 베트남을 선택한 계기 ▲한국법과 베트남법의 핵심 차이 ▲법 조문과 실제 행정 집행의 관계 ▲외국 변호사와 베트남 변호사의 역할 차이 ▲교통사고·비자·체류·임대차·투자사기·온라인 명예훼손 등 생활법률 문제 ▲문제 발생 초기 전문가 상담의 중요성 등을 다뤘다. 김 변호사는 특히 한국과 베트남의 법률·행정 시스템 차이를 강조했다. "베트남에서는 법조문뿐 아니라 지방정부와 행정기관의 실제 집행 관행, 담당 부서의 해석까지 함께 확인해야 합니다. 같은 법률 조항이라도 지역이나 담당자에 따라 집행 방식에 차이가 있을 수 있습니다." 그는 베트남의 기업 환경이 과거와 크게 달라졌다는 점도 짚었다. 과거 '느슨한 신흥시장'이라는 인식과 달리 주요 산업 분야의 규제가 촘촘해지고 집행도 엄격해지고 있는 만큼, 과거 관행에 의존하기보다 사전에 컴플라이언스 체계를 마련하고 법률 리스크를 점검해야 한다는 것이다. 생활법률 분야에서는 교통사고, 체포·구금, 임대차, 비자·체류자격, 지인 간 금전거래, 현지 파트너와의 사업, 투자사기, 온라인 명예훼손 등 교민들이 실제로 마주칠 수 있는 사례와 대응 방법을 소개했다. 김 변호사는 17년간의 베트남 현장 경험을 한 문장으로 정리했다. "현지를 존중하되 휩쓸리지 말고, 원칙을 지키되 현실을 외면하지 말자." 그는 앞으로도 베트남 진출 기업과 교민들이 법률문제에 체계적으로 대응할 수 있도록 돕고, 공익 법률 지원 활동도 이어갈 계획이라고 밝혔다.   <저작권자(c) 베트남코리아타임즈, 무단 전재-재배포 금지>

picked.t: 베트남, ‘산업생산’ 호조…8월 기준 IIP 전년동기比 11.9%↑ ‘7년 만에 최고치’
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 올 들어 베트남의 산업생산이 2019년 이후 최고치를 기록하며 호조세를 이어가고 있다. 베트남 재무부 통계국(NSO)가 지난 3일 내놓은 ‘2026년 8월 사회경제적 현황’ 보고서에 따르면, 8월 산업생산지수(IIP)는 전월 대비 1.5% 전년 동월 대비 14.4% 증가했다. 올 들어 8월 기준 평균 IIP는 전년 동기 대비 11.9% 증가해 두 자릿수 증가세를 유지했다. 이에 대해 통계국은 “8월까지 이러한 산업생산지수 증가는 최근 몇 년간 볼 수 없었던 높은 증가율”이라고 긍정 평가했다. 당국에 따르면 2019~2026년 8월 기준 9.5%를 넘은 해는 이번이 처음이다. 이러한 증가세는 전국적으로 고르게 나타나 8월 기준 전국 34개 성·시의 IIP가 모두 증가세를 보였다. 지난 8월 1일 기준 산업체 고용자 수는 전월 대비 1%, 전년 동월 대비 3.8% 증가하는 등 고용도 호조세를 유지했다. 이 같은 산업생산 가속화는 급증한 수출과 외국인직접투자(FDI) 유치와 무관치 않다는 게 경제계의 평가다. 8월 말 기준 베트남의 수출입 총액은 7,701억4,000만 달러로 전년 동기 대비 28.7% 늘어 역대 8개월 기준 최고치를 기록했다. 이 중 수출액은 3,748억 달러로 22.4% 증가했다. 원유를 포함한 외국인직접투자(FDI) 부문이 이 중 3,004억달러(80.1%)를 차지했다. 국내 경제(베트남 현지 기업) 부문은 745억달러로 7.4% 늘었다. 같은 기간 전체 수출품목 가운데 가공·산업재는 3,380억 달러로 전체의 90.2%를 차지했고, 대(對)미국 수출액은 1,220억 달러로 최대 수출 시장을 유지했다. 투자 측면에서는 8월 말 기준 베트남 내 FDI 유치액이 406억 달러로 전년 동기 대비 55.4% 늘어난 가운데 FDI 집행액 역시 172억5,000만 달러로 12% 증가했다.
